# React Wrapper (`packages/components-react/`)

React wrapper for PDS web components, plus integrations for Next.js, Remix, and React Router.

## Package Structure

```
packages/components-react/
├── src/                           # Vite dev app for testing
├── projects/
│   ├── react-wrapper/             # Generated React wrapper components
│   │   └── src/lib/components/    # {component}.wrapper.tsx files
│   ├── react-ssr-wrapper/         # SSR-compatible wrapper
│   ├── nextjs/                    # Next.js integration
│   ├── remix/                     # Remix integration
│   └── react-router/             # React Router integration
├── tests/                         # Test files
└── scripts/                       # Build scripts
```

## Wrapper Component Pattern

All wrappers follow this exact structure (generated — do not hand-edit):

```tsx
'use client';

import { forwardRef, type ForwardedRef, type JSX, type PropsWithChildren, useRef } from 'react';
import type { BaseProps } from '../../BaseProps';
import { useBrowserLayoutEffect, useMergedClass, usePrefix } from '../../hooks';
import { syncRef } from '../../utils';

export type PComponentProps = BaseProps & {
  prop1?: Type;
  prop2?: Type;
};

export const PComponent = /*#__PURE__*/ forwardRef(
  (
    { prop1 = 'default', prop2, className, ...rest }: PropsWithChildren<PComponentProps>,
    ref: ForwardedRef<HTMLElement>
  ): JSX.Element => {
    const elementRef = useRef<HTMLElement | undefined>(undefined);
    const WebComponentTag = usePrefix('p-component');

    const propsToSync = [prop1, prop2];
    useBrowserLayoutEffect(() => {
      const { current } = elementRef;
      ['prop1', 'prop2'].forEach(
        (propName, i) => ((current as any)[propName] = propsToSync[i])
      );
    }, propsToSync);

    const props = {
      ...rest,
      class: useMergedClass(elementRef, className),
      ref: syncRef(elementRef, ref),
    };

    // @ts-ignore
    return <WebComponentTag {...props} />;
  }
);
```

Key patterns:
- `'use client'` directive at top of every wrapper
- `forwardRef` with typed `P{Component}Props` extending `BaseProps`
- `usePrefix()` resolves component tag name from provider context
- `useBrowserLayoutEffect()` syncs props as element properties after mount/update
- `useMergedClass()` merges incoming `className` with web-component-set classes
- `syncRef()` handles ref forwarding
- Props are synced via `forEach` loop, not as HTML attributes

## Custom Hooks

| Hook | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `usePrefix(tagName)` | Resolve prefixed tag from `PorscheDesignSystemProvider` context |
| `useBrowserLayoutEffect(fn, deps)` | SSR-safe `useLayoutEffect` — no-op on server |
| `useMergedClass(ref, className)` | Merge React className with component-set classes |
| `useEventCallback(ref, eventName, handler)` | Bridge custom events to React callbacks |
| `useToastManager()` | Access toast API for adding messages |

## Provider Pattern

```tsx
import { PorscheDesignSystemProvider } from '@porsche-design-system/components-react';

function App() {
  return (
    <PorscheDesignSystemProvider>
      {/* Your app */}
    </PorscheDesignSystemProvider>
  );
}
```

The provider calls `load()` from `@porsche-design-system/components-js` and provides prefix context.

## SSR Usage

```tsx
// For server-side rendering (Next.js, Remix, etc.)
import { PButton, PLink } from '@porsche-design-system/components-react/ssr';

// For client-side only
import { PButton, PLink } from '@porsche-design-system/components-react';
```

## BaseProps

Defined in `projects/react-wrapper/src/lib/BaseProps.ts`:
- Omits `onChange`, `onInput`, `onToggle` to avoid conflicts with custom event bridging
- Includes standard HTML attributes and React-specific attributes
- Supports WAI-ARIA via `role` and ARIA attributes

## Event Bridging

Custom events from web components are bridged to React callbacks via `useEventCallback`:
- Controlled components (modal, flyout) require `open` prop + `onDismiss` handler
- Form components emit `onChange`, `onInput` through the bridging layer

## ARIA Usage

Use the component's `aria` prop, not direct `aria-*` attributes on the host:

```tsx
// Correct
<PButton aria={{ 'aria-label': 'Close dialog' }}>X</PButton>

// Incorrect — won't reach shadow DOM
<PButton aria-label="Close dialog">X</PButton>
```

## Framework Integrations

### Next.js (`projects/nextjs/`)
- Use `/ssr` import path for server components
- `PorscheDesignSystemProvider` in root layout

### Remix (`projects/remix/`)
- Use `/ssr` import path
- Integration with Remix routing

### React Router (`projects/react-router/`)
- Standard client-side routing integration

## Generated Files — Do Not Edit

- `dist/react-wrapper/` — build output
- `projects/react-wrapper/src/lib/components/*.wrapper.tsx` — generated by `packages/components/scripts/wrapper-generator/ReactWrapperGenerator.ts`

## Build Dependencies

Requires built first: `shared` → `tokens` → `assets` → `styles` → `utilities` → `component-meta` → `components` → `components-js`

> Commands are root workspace commands defined in the repo root `package.json`.

## Commands

```bash
npm run start:components-react              # Dev server
npm run build:components-react              # Build wrapper
npm run test:unit:components-react          # Unit tests
npm run start:components-react/nextjs       # Next.js integration
npm run start:components-react/remix        # Remix integration
npm run start:components-react/react-router # React Router integration
```
